content.comment_body: I'm looking to control the startup of a 5kVA toroidal transformer with [product_name] instead of relying on NTCs and an external relay to limit inrush current. I want a more sophisticated approach: potentially using an SSR managed by [product_name] and incorporating zero-cross detection of the line voltage. Ideally, switching the transformer when the voltage is at its peak (zero-cross + 1/4 cycle) would minimize the inrush. Premagnetizing the core with short pulses in the initial cycles could also help before applying continuous voltage. Has anyone dealt with switching these transformers? Or is sticking with NTCs still preferable for cost reasons?

If you have a line voltage detector that outputs a 0..10V analog signal (like a CT/VT), you can set up a [product_name] program with a threshold trigger on peak voltage and then implement a ramp function. The analog ramp output can tie into a PWM block to generate digital output pulses of varying lengths, as needed. For hardware, using [product_name] with transistor outputs or adding a digital output expansion could activate the SSR. However, keep in mind that these outputs are only officially rated to switch at up to 10 Hz. Actual switching speed may vary depending on the program cycle time, but it's not guaranteed by [company_name]. It's a good idea to run a simulation first to verify the setup! Have a great day—and please rate this reply.

analysis.insight_summary: The user wants to improve the method for controlling inrush current when powering a large toroidal transformer, transitioning from basic NTCs and relays to a more advanced system involving a [product_name] controller, SSR, and analog detectors. The responses outline both the customizable options possible with [product_name] and point out realtime switching limitations that may impact industrial automation scenarios needing fast, precise control.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes that the [product_name] controller will reliably execute highly accurate and rapid switching required for transformer inrush current management, ideally integrating with SSRs and analog voltage detectors for better startup performance.
pain_keywords: potential incompatibility with fast control applications
